candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — routes of administration, medication effects, and safe therapy
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — oral versus systemic vancomycin exposure
candidate.educational_objective: Explain the route-dependent use of vancomycin by distinguishing intestinal oral therapy from systemic drug exposure.

options.A: Oral vancomycin acts mainly within the intestinal tract and ordinarily does not provide reliable systemic exposure
options.B: The route difference exists only because oral vancomycin is less expensive
options.C: Oral and IV vancomycin provide essentially identical systemic exposure
options.D: Oral vancomycin is a prescribing error for C. difficile-associated diarrhea

candidate.rationale: Current vancomycin capsule labeling states that the oral product is used for C. difficile-associated diarrhea and is not effective for other types of infection because it is not ordinarily systemically absorbed. The label also notes that clinically significant absorption can occur in some patients with active colitis or inflamed intestinal mucosa, so the safest statement is that oral therapy does not provide reliable systemic exposure. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Oral vancomycin capsules are indicated for C. difficile-associated diarrhea, are not effective for other infection types because they are ordinarily not systemically absorbed, although significant absorption can occur in some patients with active colitis/inflamed mucosa.
candidate.source_locator: Warnings and Precautions 5.1 Oral Use Only; 5.2 Potential for Systemic Absorption
candidate.source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine (official FDA drug labeling)
candidate.stem: Why can oral vancomycin be used for Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea but not relied on to treat an infection at a distant systemic site?
